title: The Factories (Andhra Pradesh Amendment) Bill, 2025

summary.what_is_bill: 'The Factories (Andhra Pradesh Amendment) Bill, 2025' (L.A. Bill No. 14 of 2025) is a State legislative measure introduced in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) concerning Labour, Employment & Gig Economy.
summary.what_it_changes: The bill introduces statutory amendments to existing state legislation, primarily modifying In the Factories Act, 1948; In sub-sections (1) and (2) of the section 55 of the Principal Act; In the Principal Act across 2 identified sections/clauses.
summary.why_it_matters: According to the official Statement of Objects and Reasons: "The Factories Act, 1948 is a central legislation enacted with an objective of ensuring the safety, health and welfare of the workers employed in factories. summary.who_is_affected: Primary affected groups include: Platform & Gig Workers, App-based Aggregators / Platform Companies, Factory & Industrial Workers, Employers & Commercial Establishments, State Labour Welfare Board, Industrial Units & MSMEs.

objective: The Factories Act, 1948 is a central legislation enacted with an objective of ensuring the safety, health and welfare of the workers employed in factories. This Act has been amended several times basing on the changes in manufacturing practices, hazardous nature of manufacturing areas, changes in demographic pattern of employment, ratification of International Labour Organisation (ILO) conventions, Judicial orders, demand from industry, recommendations of DIPP to enable Ease of Doing Business etc. A meeting was held between the Secretary (Coordination), Cabinet Secretariat, Government of India and Government Andhra Pradesh and concerned Department from Government of Andhra Pradesh on reducing compliance burden and de-regulation. During the meeting Government of Andhra Pradesh informed on these amendments in line with the latest Labour Reforms undertaken by the Government of India and the way forward suggested by the Secretary (Coordination), Government of India. These reforms aim to modernize the existing framework, offering greater flexibility, while safeguarding the protection and welfare of workers.
